import pytest
from unittest.mock import Mock


class DummyContext:
    """Simple context manager that records entry and exit."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.entered = False
        self.exited = False

    def __enter__(self):
        self.entered = True
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        self.exited = True
        # Do not suppress exceptions
        return False


def test_worker_calls_run_job_and_uses_context_manager():
    # Arrange
    job = {"id": 42}
    mock_run_job = Mock()
    dummy_ctx = DummyContext()

    # Patch the globals used by _worker
    globals()["run_job"] = mock_run_job
    globals()["SLOTS"] = dummy_ctx

    # Act
    _worker(job)

    # Assert
    mock_run_job.assert_called_once_with(job)
    assert dummy_ctx.entered, "Context manager should have been entered"
    assert dummy_ctx.exited, "Context manager should have been exited"


def test_worker_propagates_exception_and_exits_context():
    # Arrange
    job = {"id": 99}
    mock_run_job = Mock(side_effect=RuntimeError("boom"))
    dummy_ctx = DummyContext()

    globals()["run_job"] = mock_run_job
    globals()["SLOTS"] = dummy_ctx

    # Act / Assert
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="boom"):
        _worker(job)

    # Ensure the job was attempted
    mock_run_job.assert_called_once_with(job)
    # Context manager must still have been entered and exited even on error
    assert dummy_ctx.entered, "Context manager should have been entered even when an exception occurs"
    assert dummy_ctx.exited, "Context manager should have been exited even when an exception occurs")
